headline: New York is widening free community college to adults aged 25 to 55 whatever their earlier education, to help workers whose jobs AI may change.
score_reason: Kept at 5: an official announcement with a clear start date, though the link to AI job losses is the governor's framing.
importance_line: It gives adults in jobs at risk from automation a tuition-free way to retrain, which matters first to those workers, then to CUNY and SUNY campuses, but the article does not show how many jobs AI is displacing in New York or how many adults will use it.
summary: The New York Daily News reports that Governor Kathy Hochul announced on Monday that from January adults aged 25 to 55 can study select high-demand associate degrees (two-year college degrees) tuition-free at the state's public CUNY and SUNY colleges, whatever their earlier education. The programme was previously open only to adults without a college degree; Hochul framed the expansion, which reaches tens of thousands more adults, as a way for people in jobs vulnerable to automation to change careers.
notes: Read in full. Official announcement quoted from statements; the New York Daily News is the outlet read, the governor's office is the origin.
